summary: Wyoming's highest fire lookout site; an L-4 cab replaced earlier tent and stone camps in the 1930s, was abandoned in 1957, and collapsed around 2010.

facts.status_note: Collapsed around 2010; OpenStreetMap and the FFLA's Wyoming list both show it gone, though the NHLR status field still reads 'standing' even as the NHLR page's own text describes the collapse.

access.note: No source describes current access or trail conditions; nothing remains to shelter in or climb.

events.note: Earliest recorded lookout staffer, Garland Toland, predating the L-4 cab, consistent with an earlier tent/stone camp on the summit.
NHLR dates the lookout's service from 1932; a Forest Service history of BTNF lookouts counts 23 years of service ending 1957, which implies a start closer to 1934. Exact build year unresolved.
Latest recorded staffer in available sources, Garland Toland.
Forest Service abandoned the lookout in favor of aerial fire detection.
Structure collapsed; NHLR gives 2010, firelookout.com gives 'early 2010s'.
Registered January 2, 2026, nominated by Dixie Boyle.

corrections.evidence: NHLR's own description text says the lookout collapsed in 2010; the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Wyoming list marks it 'Collapsed'; OpenStreetMap tags the site historic=ruins. The tower record's 'standing' value was pulled from NHLR's status field, which does not match NHLR's own page text.

sources.title: Peak into the Past With History of Wyo, BTNF Fire Lookouts

notes_for_editor: Status is likely wrong in the tower record (see correction) and should be fixed by an editor, not auto-applied. Build year is fuzzy (1932 vs. ~1934) because NHLR's stated span and the Buckrail piece's '23 years of service ending 1957' don't quite agree; left unresolved rather than guessed. No NRHP nomination form or newspaper coverage was found for this one — the two non-register sources (firelookout.com, Buckrail) carried the real narrative detail (staff names, prior tent/stone camp). Fact-check correction (2026-10-04): a draft version of the story attributed a 2000 near-miss wildfire to Wyoming Peak, citing the Buckrail article; that passage in Buckrail is actually about Deadman Fire Lookout, a different lookout covered in the same article, and has been removed.
